## How I'm categorising

`churn`, `blast_radius`, and `recency` are `0` on every finding — expected when the baseline is empty (no history to measure against). So ranking here is driven entirely by **severity × confidence × agent_risk**, and I'm layering one override on top:

| Category | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Block merge** | Wrong in any environment but the author's, OR severity ≥ 0.75 with agent_risk ≥ 0.55 in load-bearing domain code, OR *consequence exceeds score* — the finding's real-world blast radius (money, auth, false test confidence) is bigger than its numbers |
| **Warn** | Real defect, bounded impact, fix is a follow-up ticket not a gate. Typically severity 0.3–0.6, agent_risk 0.40–0.55 |
| **Ignore** | Naming/style, threshold-edge, subsumed by a blocking item, or confidence too low to spend a review cycle |

Note that severity alone gives the wrong gate list: the four `high` findings include an SVG asset (not merge-blocking), and would miss `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json` hardcoded in an API module, which is.

---

## Block merge (9)

| ID | Charge | sev / agent_risk | Why it blocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crime_00007` | Localhost-on-Disk (`src/api/files.ts:9`) | 0.60 / 0.53 | `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json` works on exactly one laptop. Every CI runner and every deploy fails. Scores say medium; consequence is total. `effort: quick`. |
| `crime_00006` | Dev-Server URL (`src/api/files.ts:8`) | 0.60 / 0.53 | Same file, same class: `localhost:3000` hardcoded in an API client. Ships an app that can only talk to the author's dev server. `effort: quick` — no reason to defer. |
| `crime_00002` | Temporal Recklessness (`src/date.ts`, 8 sites) | **0.80** / **0.62** | Highest agent_risk in the code (vs. asset) findings. A date module that reads wall time in 8 places can't be pinned in tests, and this PR ships no clock seam at all. Cheapest to fix now, before callers depend on it. |
| `crime_00003` | Half-UTC, Half-Local (`src/date.ts:9,41`) | **0.80** / **0.61** | Not hygiene — a live correctness bug. One receiver read via `getUTCFullYear()` and `getMonth()` produces dates that are wrong by the host's UTC offset, silently, only for some users. |
| `crime_00008` | Timezone Roulette (`src/date.ts:29,33`) | 0.60 / 0.53 | Same defect class, same file: `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"` resolves to a different instant per runtime. Blocking with 00002/00003 as one `date.ts` correctness fix rather than three tickets. |
| `crime_00004` | God Function `generateInvoice` (204 lines) | **0.90** / 0.55 | Highest severity in the report, 3.4× threshold, and `effort: small`. A 204-line invoice function has never been reviewed — no human is reading lines 50–253 carefully, and no agent will load the whole thing before editing. Splitting is free *now* and expensive after callers land. |
| `crime_00020` | False Identity `calculateRefundPreview` | 0.55 / 0.44 | **Consequence > score.** A function named `…Preview` calls `saveRefundAudit` and `sendRefundEmail`. Anything that "previews" a refund emails the customer and writes an audit record. Modest numbers, real incident. |
| `crime_00027` | Logic in the Alibi (`src/billing.ts:39`) | 0.50 / 0.42 | **Consequence > score.** "Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves" is an authorisation rule that exists only as prose — the detector confirms `owner`/`plan`/`billing` don't appear nearby. An unenforced auth rule sitting directly above the refund path is not a follow-up. |
| `crime_00019` | Test That Proves Nothing (0 assertions) | 0.45 / 0.46 | **Consequence > score.** This PR introduces all billing logic, and `billing.test.ts` has one test with zero `expect` calls. Green CI here means nothing, and it will be cited as coverage by the next agent. Either assert or delete. |

## Caveats on the gate

- **`suppressed_count: 1`** — one finding was filtered by config. Confirm the suppression is intentional and not hiding something in this diff.
- **Coverage is partial**: 19 files, 16 JS, 3 universal-only. This gate covers what the packs saw, not the whole PR.
- **Zeroed dimensions cut both ways.** `test_gap: 0` on the billing findings doesn't mean billing is tested — `billing.test.ts` is the file with the assertion-free test. Don't read a `0` here as a pass.
- **Nine blocks on a repo-introducing PR is high**, but seven of them are `effort: quick` or `small`. The two genuinely expensive ones (`generateInvoice` split, `date.ts` timezone unification) are the two that get dramatically more expensive once callers depend on them.
